passage: Note from Afreen and Jagdish's after-school carer. At four o'clock Jagdish took the toy train his sister Afreen was using. Her face went red and her hand shot up as if to pinch him. She stopped, clenched her fist and shouted, "Didi! Jagdish took my train!" I came over and asked each to speak in turn. Afreen said, "He can have it after I finish the track." Jagdish agreed. She still glared at him, but she stayed beside him at the track.

qa.q: What did Jagdish take from Afreen?
qa.a: He took the toy train Afreen was using.

qa.q: What was Afreen feeling when her hand shot up and then she clenched her fist?
qa.a: She was furious and wanted to win, but she also loves her brother, so she held back from pinching.

qa.q: What did Afreen do that was a wiser choice than pinching?
qa.a: She called the carer and, once asked, suggested turns: he can have the train after she finishes the track.

qa.q: How might Jagdish see the moment he took the train?
qa.a: He probably just wanted a turn and did not expect her fury. Being listened to in turn and getting the train after the track probably felt fair to him.

grounding: A sibling takes the toy I am using; I feel love and fury but call a grown-up and agree on turns.
